newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-C.BANK SEES FIRST FX SWAP AUCTION NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-C.BANK SEES FIRST FX SWAP AUCTION NEXT WEEK.

text.p: The central bank said on Tuesday it expects the first foreign exchange swap auction to take place next week.
"I expect the first auction to take place next week," Helmuts Ancans, head of the central bank's monetary policy department, told Reuters.
The central bank rules on FX swap deals, passed in April, came into effect on Tuesday.
Latvia is the first Baltic country to introduce this financial instrument, Ancans said.
"We expect the term of the swap deals initially to be three months," Ancans said.
The central bank rules set the minimum amount of a swap deal at 100,000 lats and the amount purchased/sold has to be a round figure can be divided by 10,000.
An FX swap, according to the central bank rules, involves a simultaneous purchase and sale, or vice versa, of the lat for the dollar with different spot and forward value dates.
"There is an interest amonng the commercial banks for the swap deals as it adds new possibilities to the comparatively narrow government T-bill market," Ancans said.
"Their volume is simply not sufficient," he added.
"The central bank will hold a meeting with the interested banks this Thursday to clarify all details," Ancans said.
An account held with the central bank and SWIFT membership are among conditions to qualify for the participation in an auction, the central bank rules provide.
The auctions will take place at the central bank monetary policy department market transactions' division.
